method: Hand-coded by the analyst from the OSV advisory text (and, where the text is silent, nothing else: such campaigns stay 'unknown'). Campaigns are matched by the regex in 'pattern' over OSV summary + details. Code = the execution path for someone who installs the package as a dependency. npm 12 blocking of binding.gyp ('implicit install script') was checked in npm 12.2.0 source: arborist/lib/arborist/rebuild.js sets scripts.install = node-gyp rebuild for gyp packages and then applies the same allowScripts gate.

campaigns.label: Shai-Hulud 'Here We Go Again' worm (August 2026, began with keyv/cacheable)
campaigns.pattern: Here We Go Again|keyv and cacheable
campaigns.evidence: Every poisoned release adds a preinstall hook ("preinstall": "node setup.mjs") that runs on a bare npm install, before any project code.

campaigns.label: Mini Shai-Hulud, compromised 'atool' account (@antv and others)
campaigns.evidence: Each malicious version injects a preinstall hook that executes a 498KB obfuscated Bun script.

campaigns.label: Mini Shai-Hulud, Red Hat Cloud Services trusted publisher
campaigns.evidence: The attacker injected a preinstall hook into this and 31 other packages in the @redhat-cloud-services scope.

campaigns.label: Miasma worm, LeoPlatform packages (June 2026)
campaigns.evidence: Triggered during npm install via a binding.gyp file using node-gyp command expansion; npm 12 gates the implicit gyp install script (source-checked).

campaigns.label: 'Mini Shai-Hulud is back' (TeamPCP; began with @tanstack Router/Start, 11 May 2026)
campaigns.evidence: OSV text is silent. TanStack postmortem (tanstack.com/blog/npm-supply-chain-compromise-postmortem, read 8 Oct 2026): npm resolves a malicious optionalDependencies entry pointing at a GitHub commit and runs its prepare lifecycle script; the worm 'republishes them with the same injection'. npm 12 blocks git dependencies by default (allow-git=none; observed as EALLOWGIT in the friction run). Note: with allow-git=all, npm 12.2.0 did run a git dependency's prepare step in the friction follow-up, so the allow-git default, not allowScripts, is what stops this vector. Coded 'install_only' here in the sense of 'stopped by npm 12 defaults'. Coding the whole wave from the TanStack mechanism is an assumption.

validation_of_removal_times.tanstack: Postmortem: npm removed tarballs 22:13-23:55 UTC on 11 May 2026, i.e. 2h53m-4h35m after the 19:20 UTC publish. Our packuments give no removal time for these 42 records (later clean versions exist); OSV published 23:37 UTC 11 May to 00:33 UTC 12 May.
validation_of_removal_times.cacheable: time.modified gives 1.28 h; OSV published 1.29 h after publish.
validation_of_removal_times.antv_attr: time.modified gives 3,006.8 h (about 125 days) for a Mini Shai-Hulud version; OSV published within minutes of publish. time.modified is therefore unreliable for established packages, which receive later metadata edits.
